expect.note: an exception the judge module does not define (not JudgeError) still fails the run closed; and `stub_judge`'s verdict vocabulary is CLOSED — the four recognised forms behave and anything else raises ValueError rather than certifying

provenance: M36 acceptance criterion 2 says 'judge error, timeout, missing API key, malformed response, budget exhausted' -- an open-ended list, not a closed one. `judge-fail-closed-on-error` proves `JudgeError` specifically; this proves the boundary is `except Exception`, not `except JudgeError`, by handing `_apply_judge` a judge callable that raises a bare `ValueError` it has never heard of. A narrower catch (matching only JudgeError, mirroring `live_planner`'s deliberately narrow `PlanError` distinction in planner.py) would let this propagate uncaught -- which would still not be a false 'success' in THIS repo's call graph (server.py's outer catch-all and the eval harness's own top-level exception handling both turn an uncaught raise into a non-success result too), but it would mean fail-closed is an accident of what happens to wrap `run_task`, not a property `_apply_judge` itself guarantees. The distinction planner.py draws between PlanError (the model's fault) and everything else (a transport fault, scored differently by the ablation) does NOT apply here on purpose: the judge has no equivalent to 'the model answered with prose' that needs separating from 'the call failed' -- every failure mode is the same verdict, FAIL. Extended 2026-08-28 with `stub_vocabulary`, closing T-M39-1 (P1). `stub_judge` read a verdict as `certify, reason = v if isinstance(v, (tuple, list)) else (v, "stub")` after its two string branches, so ANY other string was coerced by `bool()` — and a non-empty string is True. A case that mistyped its token (`"maformed"`, `"reject"`, `"fail"`) got a CERTIFYING judge, and if it expected a failure it reported that failure as the code's fault rather than its own typo. This is PR #33 R1's exact defect — truthiness inverting fail-closed — one level up, in the stub the whole `fast` suite runs on: R1 was fixed in `live_judge`'s parser and the stub was never looked at. It raises `ValueError`, not `JudgeError`, and the probe asserts which: a mistyped token is the CASE's fault, and `JudgeError` would be swallowed by the very fail-closed path this case's other half grades, turning a typo into a plausible-looking rejected verdict. The empty string is in the typo list because it is the one unrecognised value `bool()` would have coerced the OTHER way, and a vocabulary check that only tries truthy junk proves half a rule. Watched red: all five typo payloads returned `certify=True` (or `False` for `""`) instead of raising.

triage.note: guards against narrowing the except clause to `JudgeError` only, which would be the natural thing to copy from planner.py's PlanError precedent and would be wrong here.
